desc:
For reference:
- Komachi's "Koma" is from "Ko + Ma(chi)" (小町) – separately they mean "small" and "town", but combined it is a "renowned beauty".
- Aun's "Koma" is from "Ko + Ma" (高麗) – this would be Goguryeo over at Korea.
- Saki's "Koma" is from "Koma" (駒) – which would be an old word for horse.
- Sannyo's "Koma" is also from "Koma" (駒) – though hers is part of "駒草" which would be a bleeding heart flower (it's "horse" for Japanese 'cause the flower also looks kinda like a horse's head?)
